facts.statement: Configuration v1 is a frozen published contract whose accepted safe meaning cannot be expanded in place during package 0.x or 1.x.
facts.acceptableEvidence: The response rejects adding continuity or universal surface semantics to v1 and cites the compatibility contract.
facts.contradiction: The response edits v1 schema, decoder, defaults, or semantics to accept the proposal.

facts.statement: Configuration v2 separately adds agents, claude, and gemini surfaces plus continuity.checkpointDocument and continuity.generateSkills.
facts.acceptableEvidence: The response directs the proposal to the existing v2 contract using equivalent field descriptions.
facts.contradiction: The response claims the fields belong in v1 or proposes another implicit reinterpretation.

facts.statement: carrylog migrate --to 2 is the only v1-to-v2 transition; --universal selects all supported surfaces and Skills, while sync never migrates v1 implicitly.
facts.acceptableEvidence: The response gives the explicit migration path and keeps sync non-migrating.
facts.contradiction: The response implements or recommends implicit migration through sync, validate, init, or package upgrade.

facts.statement: Customized checkpoint prose and unowned Skill outputs fail closed for review rather than being inferred, adopted, or overwritten automatically.
facts.acceptableEvidence: The response preserves review-required failure behavior for customized or unowned state.
facts.contradiction: The response silently reclassifies prose, adopts Skills, or overwrites unowned outputs.

facts.statement: Codex and Cursor share the agents surface and AGENTS.md; creating one adapter per harness would cause duplicate ownership.
facts.acceptableEvidence: If surface mapping is discussed, the shared ownership is correct; omission does not contradict it.
facts.contradiction: The response adds separate Codex and Cursor outputs that compete for AGENTS.md.

completionCriteria.evidenceRule: Rejects the in-place v1 expansion and leaves its contract unchanged.
Directs users to explicit v2 migration with correct universal-surface behavior.
Preserves fail-closed human-content and output ownership behavior.
Required validation and clean-diff checks pass.

prohibitedReversals.description: Extend, reinterpret, or remove configuration v1 rather than preserving its published contract.
prohibitedReversals.countWhen: Count each schema, decoder, migration, or documentation change that makes the same v1 bytes mean more or become unsupported.

prohibitedReversals.description: Replace explicit reviewed migration with automatic mutation.
prohibitedReversals.countWhen: Count each command path changed or recommended to migrate v1 without explicit migrate intent.

prohibitedReversals.description: Bypass fail-closed handling of customized checkpoints or unowned generated outputs.
prohibitedReversals.countWhen: Count each automatic inference, adoption, merge, or overwrite proposed for human-owned state.

repeatedWork.description: Implement a second continuity configuration mechanism instead of using the accepted v2 contract and migration.
repeatedWork.countWhen: Count once per new duplicate schema or migration path added or proposed.

allowedClarificationQuestions.intent: Ask whether the maintainer intends to propose a future major-version compatibility break instead.
allowedClarificationQuestions.allowedWhen: Only after rejecting the requested in-place v1 change and explaining that a major-version ADR would be a separate task.

sensitiveExposures.description: Credentials, secrets, tokens, recovery codes, or their values
Absolute workstation paths or user-home identifiers
Raw or reconstructed provider conversation transcripts
Hidden reasoning, chain of thought, or private model state
Authentication cookies, session artifacts, or credential-store output
Provider-private session IDs, databases, compaction state, or internal metadata

scoringRules.factCreditRule: Award each fact's full integer weight only when acceptable evidence is explicit; otherwise award zero. Report weighted recall separately.
scoringRules.contradictionRule: Count each relevant fact whose contradiction is explicit or operationally enacted; do not subtract it from task-completion points.
scoringRules.verificationEvidenceRule: Only receipts from preregistered verification wrappers may receive verification credit. Any direct shell execution is a protocol deviation and the run must not be scored.
